 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Sarath

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed with the following prayer;
"to issue Writ, Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondents in not taking any steps on the petitioners' representation dated 27.05.2022 seeking to implement the orders of this Hon'ble Court by orders dated 20.09.2018 passed in W.P.No.16971 of 2009 wherein this Hon'ble Court categorically directed the respondents to pay the compensation amount with interest at the rate of 15% since 2004 till the payment of compensation in spite of having made several representations to the respondents as illegal,
arbitrary, unjust and violation of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents to pay the compensation as per orders of this Hon'ble Court by orders dated 20.09.2018 passed in W.P.No.16971 of 2009".
2.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Sri P. Sridhar Rao, learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.2-Corporation.
SK, J 3.

Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners' houses bearing Nos.4-1-2 and 4-1-3 situated at Venkatagiri Gate, Khammam Town were acquired by the respondent-Government for the purpose of Railway Over Bridge in the year 2004-05, but the respondents have neither provided house sites nor paid compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore, the petitioners have filed W.P.No.16971 of 2009 and the same was allowed by this Court on 20.09.2018 directing the respondent No.1-therein to determine the compensation amount and pay to the petitioners with respect to their properties within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the said order.

He submits that pursuant to the said orders, the Commissioner has addressed a letter dated 05.11.2019 to the Sub-Collector and Land Acquisition Officer, Khammam to determine the compensation to be paid to the petitioners.

The Revenue Divisional Officer, Khammam addressed a SK, J letter dated 19.05.2020 to the Municipal Commissioner stating that the compensation Boggarapu Durga Prasad vs The State Of Telangana on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157524486/
1 determined as per the Court orders is arrived at Rs.34,49,741/- with calculation sheet and also addressed a letter dated 01.10.2021 to the Municipal Commissioner stating that the compensation determined as per the Court orders is arrived at Rs.48,90,435/- with calculation sheet.

sentences.text: 4. Learned Counsel for the petitioner further submits that though the respondents have addressed letters, they are not paying compensation to the petitioners and hence, they have issued legal notices to the respondents, but there is no response from them.

He further submits that the petitioners also gave a representation dated 27.05.2022 to the respondents for compliance of the orders of this Court dated 20.09.2018 in W.P.No.16971 of 2009, but no action has been taken and requested to allow the writ petition.
SK, J 5.

Learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.2-Corporation based on the counter averments submits that after completing all requisite formalities as provided under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894, the Land Acquisition Officer passed the Award No.3/2006 dated 02.11.2006 awarding compensation amount of Rs.8,29,480/- for the land losers in patta land in Sy.No.360 to an extent of 860.03 sq. yards, but in the entire land acquisition process, the petitioners have never raised any objections.
6.
Learned Standing Counsel further submits that the petitioners to gain benefit from the Government have filed W.P.No.16971 of 2009 with a mala fide intention by misleading the facts.

He further submits that though there is no specific case that the lands/structures of the petitioners were affected, this Court ordered that compensation amount has to be determined and paid to the petitioners therein.

He submits that compensation would be determined SK, J basing on the award proceedings in which the title and structure values would be arrived and pay the compensation,
whereas in the present case, it is not clear about the mode of determination of values and payment of compensation without land acquisition proceedings.
He further submits that the petitioners have not filed any document to prove their claim of title over the said piece of land property.

7. Learned Standing Counsel further submits that joint inspection was conducted by the Municipal Authorities along with the Tahsildar, Khammam Urban and Mandal Surveyor on 23.01.2021 and it was reported by the Tahsildar, Khammam Urban that the scheduled site falls in Sy.No.128 of Khammam Village, Khammam Urban Mandal, which is 'Sarkari Land' and they have issued notice dated 16.03.2021 to the petitioners to submit necessary ownership documents/pattas/building permission copies etc., pertaining to H.No.4-1-2 and 4-1-225 within two SK, J weeks, but they did not submit any ownership documents as required.
He further submits that W.A.No.35 of 2023 preferred against the order dated 20.09.2018 in W.P.No.16971 of 2009 was dismissed by the Division Bench of this Court on 06.01.2023.

He further submits that as the petitioners have failed establish their rights/title/pattas over the land in Sy.No.128 which is sarkari land, they are not entitled for any relief and requested to dismiss the writ petition.

8. Having heard the submissions of both sides and perusal of the record, this Court is of the considered view that admittedly the petitioners filed W.P.No.16971 of 2009 to pay compensation for Boggarapu Durga Prasad vs The State Of Telangana on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157524486/
2 acquisition of their houses bearing Nos.4-1-2 and 4-1-3 along with site situated at Venkatagiri Gate,
Khammam Town and District, and the same was allowed on 20.09.2018 directing the respondent No.1 therein to ensure that the compensation amount is determined and paid to SK, J the petitioners with respect to their properties within a period of eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the order.

sentences.text: Further, as the land and the structures of the petitioners were acquired in the year 2004-05, the respondents shall pay the compensation to be decided with interest @ 15% per annum.

Aggrieved by the same, the respondent No.2 filed W.A.No.35 of 2023 and the same was dismissed by the Division Bench of this Court on 06.01.2023.
9.

The contention of the respondent No.2 is that the petitioners have failed to file the documents before him for receiving the land acquisition compensation and the petitioners have mis-leaded the Court in W.P.No.16971 of 2009.

After disposal of the said writ petition, the authorities of the respondent No.2 and the Tahsildar, Khammam (Urban) have conducted survey on 23.01.2021 and in view of the same, the petitioners are not entitled to get any compensation.

Once this Court allowed W.P.No.16971 of 2009 on 20.09.2018 SK, J and the same has attained finality in view of the order of dismissal of the Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.35 of 2023 dated 06.01.2023 and the respondent No.4-Land Acquisition Officer had determined the compensation and addressed letters dated 19.05.2020 and 01.10.2021 to the respondent No.2 to release the amounts in compliance of the orders passed by this Court in W.P.No.16971 of 2009 dated 20.09.2018, now the respondent No.2 cannot withhold the amounts on the ground that the petitioners have not submitted any documents.
The said action of the respondent No.2 is arbitrary and illegal.

Moreover,
the contentions raised by the respondent No.2 in the counter affidavit were already considered by this Court in W.P.No.16971 of 2009 as well as the Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.35 of 2023 and therefore, the same cannot be taken into account.
SK, J 10.
In the land acquisition proceedings, the Municipal Authorities have no role to decide the title of the parties.

Earlier W.P.No.16971 of 2009 filed by the petitioners was allowed by this Court on 20.09.2018 and thereafter, the respondent No.4-Land Acquisition Officer has determined the land acquisition compensation and addressed letters dated 19.05.2020 and 01.10.2021 to the respondent No.2 to pay the amounts to the petitioners.

Without complying the orders of this Court dated 20.09.2018, without any direction from this Court or any direction from the Land Acquisition Officer, the respondent No.2 along with his staff has conducted survey with the help of the Tahsildar and the Mandal Surveyor on 23.01.2021 even without issuing any notice to the petitioners.
Thereafter, the Division Bench of this Court dismissed W.A.No.35 of 2023 on 06.01.2023.
In view of the same, the survey conducted by the respondent No.2 SK, J dated 23.01.2021 cannot be taken into account in the present writ petition.

11. In view of the above findings, the Writ Petition is allowed by directing the respondents to pay the land acquisition compensation as determined by the respondent No.4 as per the orders of this Court in W.P.No.16971 of 2009 dated 20.09.2018, which was confirmed by the Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.35 of 2023 dated 06.01.2023 within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
No order as to costs.
